lessons_used: Home wait_info changes are helpful, winning 4 out of 8 tests.
Adoption redesigns are helpful, winning both tests with strong positive results.
Choose_path copy updates and redesigns showed no positive effect, ranging from no clear effect to performing worse across 2 tests each.
Finish hints, sign-in notifications, and sign-in redesigns showed no positive effect, ranging from no clear effect to performing worse across 2 tests each.
Adoption hints (3 tests), home redesigns (2 tests), finish layouts (2 tests), finish new flows (2 tests), sign-in copy updates (2 tests), and sign-in incentives (2 tests) showed no clear effect.
Predictions were systematically too low for winning changes and too high for changes with no clear effect or negative results; single-test categories remain thin evidence.

candidates.title: Adoption Certificate Two Column Split Redesign
candidates.change: Rebuild the adoption certificate layout into a side-by-side split layout showing companion traits on one side and registration details on the other.
candidates.why: Adoption redesigns have a strong record of success (winning both previous tests), and the adoption step takes a median of 89s with an 80.8% conversion rate.

components.text: Your new companion is officially registered to your desktop habitat.

guard.reason: The redesigned components remove the required official stamp from the adoption certificate.

candidates.title: Waiting Screen Habitat Sound & Activity Timer Layout
candidates.change: Add ambient habitat sound indicators and visual progress tracking to the waiting screen while pet generation finishes.
candidates.why: Home wait_info improvements have won 4 out of 8 tests previously, helping users remain engaged during the high mean home wait time of 2336s.

guard.reason: Valid waiting screen enhancement with progress tracking and ambient audio.

candidates.score_note: Home step drop-off is low (7%), but home wait_info has a solid track record (+1.9% historical average over 8 tests).

candidates.title: Desktop Pet Quick Command Cheat Sheet Screen
candidates.change: Add a dedicated quick command cheat sheet screen at the end of onboarding that highlights hotkeys for controlling, talking to, and hiding the pet.
candidates.why: Support mail highlights 3 complaints about users being confused on how to control or hide their desktop pet post-onboarding.

new_command_cheatsheet.headline: Quick Companion Desktop Commands
new_command_cheatsheet.body: Learn how to summon, feed, or hide your companion anytime using simple desktop hotkeys.

components.text: Press Alt+P to toggle desktop visibility

guard.reason: Valid addition of a new cheat sheet screen following home intro.

candidates.score_note: Supported by 3 support emails, but adding a new screen to finish historical tests showed negligible lift (+0.2%) and has high build cost.

candidates.title: Desktop Habitat Preparation Interactive Preview Flow
candidates.change: Introduce a interactive preview flow on the waiting screen enabling users to explore desktop habitat sounds and themes while pet generation finishes.
candidates.why: The home wait step exhibits a long mean time of 2336s; providing interactive habitat previews keeps users engaged.

waiting.headline: Preparing Your Pet Desktop Habitat
waiting.body: Preview desktop habitat sounds and themes while your custom pet finishes generating.

guard.reason: Valid interactive preview flow added to the waiting screen.

candidates.score_note: Home wait time is long, but interactive new flows on home previously lost conversion (-0.4%) and require full UI development.

candidates.title: Waiting Screen Ambient Audio Activity Hint
candidates.change: Display an ambient audio hint on the waiting screen reassuring users that pet rendering is actively working in the background.
candidates.why: Home wait_info features are proven winners (4 of 8 tests), reassuring users during long generation times.

waiting.hint: Listen closely to hear your pet getting ready in its background desktop habitat!

guard.reason: Valid hint and progress indicator added to the waiting screen.

candidates.score_note: Home wait_info features consistently succeed (4/8 wins, +1.9% lift) and simple hint additions are lightweight config changes.

candidates.title: Pick Friend Full Bleed Gallery Redesign
candidates.change: Redesign the companion selection step into a full bleed gallery layout showcasing high-resolution pet animations.
candidates.why: Adoption screen redesigns have consistently yielded strong positive results in past iterations.

guard.reason: Valid full-bleed redesign of the pet selection screen.

candidates.score_note: Adoption redesigns are proven strong winners (2/2 tests won, +9.5% lift), though creating full gallery screens requires high implementation cost.

candidates.title: Adoption Certificate Desktop Placement Reassurance Hint
candidates.change: Add an explicit hint on the adoption certificate reassuring users that their pet will automatically appear on their desktop taskbar once ready.
candidates.why: Support receives multiple tickets (3 emails) reporting pets missing from the desktop after setup.

adoption_certificate.hint: Your companion will appear directly on your desktop taskbar once setup is complete.

guard.reason: Valid reassurance hint added to the adoption certificate screen.

candidates.score_note: Addresses repeated support mail feedback at low cost, but adoption hints have consistently shown no positive effect (-1.0% across 3 tests).

candidates.title: Home Intro Desktop Controls Quick Reference Copy
candidates.change: Update headline and body on the final home intro screen to explain how to summon, control, and hide the pet on the desktop.
candidates.why: 3 support emails reported user confusion regarding how to control, hide, or talk to their pet after finishing onboarding.

home_intro.headline: Welcome Your Companion to Your Desktop
home_intro.body: Right-click your pet anytime to hide, access settings, or start a voice interaction.

guard.reason: Valid copy update explaining pet controls on the home intro screen.

candidates.score_note: Low cost text update directly backed by 3 support emails, though finish step text/hint tweaks historically yield neutral to negative results.

candidates.title: Waiting Screen Completion Notification Toggle
candidates.change: Enable an explicit desktop notification prompt on the pet generation waiting screen so users know when generation finishes.
candidates.why: Home step drop-off occurs during long wait times (mean 2336s); desktop notifications alert users when rendering completes.

waiting.headline: Pet Generation in Progress
waiting.body: We will send a desktop notification as soon as your companion is ready to meet you.

guard.reason: Valid completion notification toggle added to the waiting screen.

candidates.score_note: Targets long home wait times, but notification prompts generally underperform in onboarding tests.

candidates.title: Story Screen Card Carousel Layout
candidates.change: Switch the story screen layout to a card carousel presentation to engage users before path selection.
candidates.why: The choose_path step has a 76.2% conversion rate and a mean time of 514s; improving the initial story layout improves engagement.

story.headline: Welcome to Desktop Pets
story.body: Swipe to explore how your desktop pet lives and interacts with your workspace.

guard.reason: Valid carousel redesign of the story screen introducing the pet.

candidates.score_note: Targets a high drop-off step (23.8% lost), but choose_path layout changes previously regressed step conversion (-3.9%).

lessons_next: Home wait_info changes are consistently helpful, winning 5 out of 9 tests.
Adoption redesigns are generally helpful, winning 2 out of 3 tests.
Choose_path updates (copy, layout, redesign) showed no positive effect, ranging from no clear effect to performing worse across multiple tests.
Finish hints, sign-in notifications, and sign-in redesigns showed no positive effect, frequently leading to negative impacts or early test stops.
Adoption hints, home redesigns, finish layouts, finish new flows, sign-in copy, and sign-in incentives showed no clear effect across 2 or 3 tests each.
Predictions were systematically too low for big winning changes and too high for changes with no clear effect or negative outcomes; single-test categories remain thin evidence.
